findings.title: "Silence notifications" does nothing in the Grafana rule list
findings.body: The Grafana list now renders `RuleActionsButtons` with only `promRule` (`GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47`), so `rule` is undefined. `AlertRuleMenu` computes `canSilence` from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (`AlertRuleMenu.tsx:96`) and shows the item. Its `onClick` calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`. The drawer only renders if `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. `rule` is undefined here, so that is always false. `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` takes a `rulerRule` prop and reads `rulerRule.grafana_alert.uid` (`SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer.tsx:12,21`). The user clicks the menu item and nothing happens, with no error. The new test only checks that the item is present (`GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:194`), not that it works. The drawer needs to be driven from `promRule`, or the item hidden when there is no ruler rule.

findings.title: Delete and Pause menu items silently disappear for Grafana rules in the list view
findings.body: `canPause` and `canDelete` now include the prom-based ability. The rendering is still gated on a ruler rule. Pause needs `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). Delete needs `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165). The Grafana list view no longer fetches ruler rules, so `rulerRule` is always undefined. The abilities are computed from `promRule` and then ignored. A user with delete/update permission on the folder no longer sees Pause or Delete on any rule in the new list. `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:205-207` shows this: it grants delete and update permissions and expects only 4 items. The PR description does not call this out. Either build these actions from `promRule` (`MenuItemPauseRule` and the delete modal take an identifier or uid) or document the removal. Otherwise the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` calls for Pause and Delete are dead code.

findings.title: View link no longer carries `returnTo`
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleListItem` built the href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new one drops it: `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)`. The sibling `DataSourceRuleListItem.tsx:36-42` still passes `returnTo`. The rule viewer uses it to send the user back to the filtered or paginated list they came from, so Grafana-managed rules lose that behaviour. Restore `createReturnTo()` in the href.

findings.title: Test pins the loss of Pause and Delete as expected behaviour
findings.body: The test grants AlertingRuleUpdate and AlertingRuleDelete in `beforeEach`, then asserts `menuItems.length` is exactly 4 (silence, copy link, duplicate, export). Its comment says "all 4 menu actions should be available". Delete and Pause are missing from that list because of the regression in `AlertRuleMenu`. The test will fail if someone restores those actions. The Silence assertion only checks that the item exists, not that clicking it opens the drawer. Add a click test for Silence and assert Delete and Pause explicitly once they are fixed.

findings.title: Dead `operation` prop and stale preload comment
findings.body: No caller passes `operation` any more. The Creating and Deleting states were removed from `GrafanaGroupLoader`, and `FilterView` never passed it. The prop can go. In `prometheusGroupsGenerator.ts` the comment at line 81 still says "preload ruler rules" and the variable at line 84 is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`, but the ruler prefetch was removed. Rename both.

contracts.action: Grafana rule list rows render actions from promRule only (no ruler rule)
contracts.equivalent_path: The removed GrafanaRuleListItem in GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx passed `rule={rulerRule}` and `promRule`. Every action in AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons.V2 then had a ruler rule available.
contracts.before_after: Before: the ruler rule drove the Edit link, Pause, Delete and the Silence drawer. After: only Edit (uid identifier) and Duplicate/Export/Silence-item visibility work. Pause and Delete are gated on `rulerRule` and Silence's drawer on `rule`, so none of them work.
contracts.visible_effect: Pause and Delete vanish from the More menu. Silence is shown but clicking it does nothing.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent: no error and no log. Permission checks pass, then the UI gates drop the action.

contracts.equivalent_path: useAllRulerRuleAbilities with useIsRuleEditable and useCanSilence (useAbilities.ts:231, useIsRuleEditable.ts:18, useAbilities.ts:560)
contracts.before_after: The prom path uses the same folder-metadata checks (`hasPermissionInMetadata` on the folder from useFolder). It drops the ruler-availability discovery. It treats Grafana as always supported. Silence no longer waits for the folder to load. Provenance comes from the new `provenance` field, which the backend sets on prom rules (`api_prometheus.go:708`).
contracts.visible_effect: Edit, Duplicate and Export visibility match the ruler path for Grafana rules; provisioned rules are immutable.
contracts.failure_mode: If the folder fetch fails, `isEditable` is false and Edit is hidden. There is no error shown, the same as the existing ruler path.

contracts.action: FilterView renders GrafanaRuleListItem directly from the filtered prom rule (no per-rule ruler/prom group fetch)
contracts.equivalent_path: The removed GrafanaRuleLoader fetched the ruler group and the prom group per rule, showed a skeleton, and showed an error alert on failure.
contracts.before_after: Before: per-rule loading and error states. After: it renders at once from data already fetched. The `returnTo` query param is lost on the view link. Cannot-load-rule error alerts and their i18n strings were removed.
contracts.visible_effect: Faster list with fewer requests; view links lose returnTo.
contracts.failure_mode: Group fetch errors are now handled only at the group or filter level.

summary: The Grafana rule list now builds its row actions from the prom rule only, because the ruler fetch was removed. The permission side was migrated (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` and related hooks) but the actions behind it were not, so the user-facing behaviour regresses in three ways: (1) the \"Silence notifications\" item is shown but clicking it opens nothing, because the drawer needs a ruler rule; (2) Pause and Delete no longer appear in the menu, because both are gated on `rulerRule`; (3) the rule view link lost `returnTo`. The new test pins the 4-item menu, so it locks in the Pause/Delete loss. There are also small cleanups: a dead `operation` prop and a stale \"ruler preload\" comment and variable name. I read the changed files in full, but the repository code was not run."
